title: CpG content contributes to tissue-resident macrophage enhancer selection.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Opened the GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) series record and its machine-readable file manifest (filelist.txt) for GSE317131: 23 samples, and every processed file is a genome coverage track - 8 ATAC-seq (assay for transposase-accessible chromatin) and 2 ChIP-seq files in IGV's binary TDF format (35-99 MB each) plus 12 RNA-seq bigWig files (55-80 MB each), with one 1.5 GB RAW.tar. There is no peak table, no count matrix and no differential-region table anywhere in the deposit. I also opened the article's full text and its XML, which lists exactly one supplementary item, gkag824_supplemental_files.zip; I failed to retrieve it through four routes (Europe PMC supplementaryFiles timed out twice, PMC /bin/ returned the 1,817-byte challenge page, Europe PMC fulltextRepo returned HTTP 500, PMC open-access package service returned 404).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: All region counts come from the Methods text, not from a file I opened: an initial consensus peak set of 173,596 fixed 100-base-pair peaks and a final tissue-resident-macrophage set of 64,490 promoter-distal peaks, quantified as decile-normalised RPKM (reads per kilobase per million mapped reads). The existence and contents of Supplementary Tables S9/S10 (clusters of regions specific to exactly one macrophage population) and S19 (list of public datasets reused) are known only from the text.

a1_downloadable.note: GSE317131 is public with no login (manifest and metadata opened directly). The supplementary zip is also openly posted at the journal, but I could not retrieve it through four routes in this session - a tooling failure, not an access restriction.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL, verified in the manifest. The target (is this region open specifically in alveolar macrophages, in another tissue-resident macrophage, or in bone-marrow-derived macrophages?) is not a column in anything downloadable: GEO holds only binary coverage tracks, so the label would have to be built by MACS2 peak calling, consensus-peak merging and differential analysis - starting from raw FASTQ sequencing reads, which this project does not download. The supplementary tables may hold the region clusters, but I could not open them to check.

a3_inputs_present.note: No per-region table exists in the deposit, so there are no coordinates to turn into sequence; even with the supplementary tables, DNA sequence is absent and would need extraction from the mm10 mouse reference genome (~2.6 GB). Not verified - stopped at A2.

a4_units_stated.note: Methods state units clearly (decile-normalised RPKM for chromatin accessibility, FPKM for expression), but no file with those values was downloadable or opened.

a5_enough_rows.note: Paper text implies tens of thousands of 100-base-pair regions (173,596 initial, 64,490 final promoter-distal consensus peaks). I verified no row count in any file; n_rows is therefore null.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 1.5 GB RAW.tar of coverage tracks; reprocessing would need SRA FASTQ files (tens of GB) plus mm10
a6_fits_laptop.note: Because A2 forces re-deriving the label, the real working set is raw sequencing data plus alignment, which is neither laptop-scale nor allowed here. Not verified - stopped at A2.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked: there is no table in the deposit whose row count could be compared with the paper's 173,596 / 64,490 figures.

a8_label_provenance.note: The label would trace back to a physical measurement (Tn5 transposase accessibility), not to another model's output, so A8 itself is fine; the problem is that the measurement is only distributed as smoothed coverage tracks.

existing_models.name: ChromBPNet models trained on alveolar macrophage ATAC-seq (used in a 2025/2026 study of tissue-resident versus monocyte-derived alveolar macrophages, PMC12934662)
existing_models.score_and_split: Five models trained on five chromosome-based folds (different train/validation/test chromosome groups), with a custom Tn5 cut-bias model regressed out; exact accuracy numbers not retrieved, only the abstract-level description from search results.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrieved - I read only the search summary, not the paper's discussion.

existing_models.name: AI-TAC, a convolutional neural network predicting chromatin accessibility across 81 mouse immune cell types from sequence (Maslova et al., PNAS 2020)
existing_models.score_and_split: Predicts per-region accessibility across 81 immune populations including macrophages; code and weights at github.com/smaslova/AI-TAC. I did not retrieve its reported accuracy or split, so no number is claimed.

existing_models.name: Bag-of-Motifs, gradient-boosted trees on transcription-factor motif counts for cell-type-specific distal regulatory elements (Nature Communications 2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported accurate prediction of cell-type-specific enhancers across several species; numbers and split not retrieved.

existing_models.name: CREsted, a framework for modelling cell-type-specific enhancers across tissues and species (Nature Methods 2026)
existing_models.score_and_split: Presented as a general toolkit for sequence models of cell-type-specific enhancer activity; numbers not retrieved.

backbone.name: Nucleotide Transformer / DNABERT-2 / HyenaDNA (open DNA language models) would fit 100-base-pair to 1-kilobase regions, and AlphaGenome is available non-commercially
backbone.hardware: CPU embedding of ~60,000 short regions is feasible overnight; training a head is minutes
backbone.licence: Nucleotide Transformer and DNABERT-2 are openly licensed; AlphaGenome is non-commercial

integration.partner_dataset: ImmGen ATAC atlas (chromatin accessibility across 81 mouse immune cell types) and ENCODE mouse whole-genome bisulphite methylation data, joinable on mm10 genomic coordinates
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does the CpG-rich versus CpG-poor split that separates alveolar from bone-marrow-derived macrophage enhancers generalise across all 81 immune cell types, or is it specific to tissue residency? - a good question, but it needs a region table this deposit does not provide.

controls.positive_control: A model must recover CpG dinucleotide fraction as the dominant feature, since the paper shows that single number separates the two enhancer classes - which is also why the model adds little.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle region labels and confirm collapse to the majority class; also train on CpG percentage alone to see how much of the signal one trivial feature explains.
controls.external_validation: ImmGen ATAC atlas and other tissue-resident macrophage ATAC datasets listed in Supplementary Table S19 (microglia, Kupffer cells, peritoneal macrophages) - but those are the same public sets the paper already used for its labels.

honest_claim_h3: A sequence model here could claim only that it separates 100-base-pair regions called open in alveolar macrophages from those called open in cultured bone-marrow-derived macrophages, in female mice from one laboratory, using regions that the authors' own peak-calling pipeline defined - and that CpG content alone does most of that separation.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use DNA sequence to predict whether a regulatory region is open in lung-resident macrophages or in cultured blood-derived macrophages.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example would be a 100-base-pair to 1-kilobase stretch of mouse genome around an accessible-chromatin peak, represented as its DNA letters. The paper's Methods imply roughly 64,490 promoter-distal regions, but I verified no count in any file.
plain_idea.predict: A label saying which macrophage population the region is open in. The truth comes from ATAC-seq, which cuts DNA where chromatin is loose, followed by the authors' peak calling and differential-accessibility analysis.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Immunologists studying why cultured macrophages never fully become tissue macrophages would learn which sequence features gate enhancer use; even a failed model would quantify how much of enhancer identity is sequence-encoded versus environment-driven.

more_or_better_data.why: Eight ATAC-seq samples (two replicates per condition) from one laboratory, one mouse strain, one sex. AI-TAC was trained on the ImmGen atlas spanning 81 immune cell types, and ChromBPNet alveolar macrophage models already exist; this deposit adds no scale.

confidence_score.why: Only two ATAC replicates per condition, and the deposit contains no per-region values at all, so replicate-level noise cannot even be estimated from what is downloadable.

models_beatable.why: The competing models are recent and honestly evaluated: ChromBPNet alveolar macrophage models use five chromosome-held-out folds with Tn5 cut-bias correction, and AI-TAC (2020) ships open weights for 81 mouse immune populations.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition - we have no feature/label table to run any baseline on, since the processed data are coverage tracks rather than quantified regions.

ml_idea: Classify mouse accessible-chromatin regions as alveolar-macrophage-specific, other-tissue-resident-macrophage-specific or bone-marrow-derived-macrophage-specific from DNA sequence alone, using a frozen DNA language model plus a small head, and test whether anything beyond CpG dinucleotide content carries the signal.

effort.compute_note: No estimate is honest here: the deposit has no quantified regions, so the real first step is re-aligning raw sequencing reads and re-running MACS2 peak calling - a server job, not a laptop job. Nothing was timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: List the GEO supplementary files (one request): if every processed file is a coverage track rather than a peak or count table, the label has to be rebuilt from raw reads and the project is dead. That is exactly what happened.

verdict_reason: Part A2 fails in the files: GSE317131 ships only IGV TDF and bigWig coverage tracks, so the cell-type-specificity label would have to be reconstructed by peak calling and differential analysis from raw sequencing reads; the supplementary tables that might contain the regions were not retrievable through four routes. Even granting the best case, the task (sequence predicting cell-type-specific accessibility in mouse macrophages) is already served by open, chromosome-split-evaluated models - ChromBPNet alveolar macrophage models and AI-TAC - and the paper's own result says one trivially computed feature, CpG content, carries most of the signal.
